newsitem.title: UK: Australia's Howard wants to raise growth potential.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard wants to raise growth potential.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday he wanted to increase his country's savings and growth potential and that the government planned to almost halve its net debt by the year 2000.
Howard, in a speech to the Confederation of British Industry, also said Australia was over-reliant on income tax as a revenue source.
He added he was opposed to any legally-binding emission targets as that would reduce Australia's growth by two percent by the year 2010.
Howard said the Australian economy was "strong" and that the country's future prospects were "exceedingly strong".
He said there was "an over-reliance on income tax as a source of revenue" and an "unacceptably high level of taxation at the marginal rate" which was denting incentive.
He also was opposed to European Union proposoals for legally binding targets for OECD countries to cut the emission of greenhouse gasses by 2010.
"The proposals the UK and the EU are pursuing would have an adverse effect on the Australian economy," Howard said. "(This) would cost us two percent of GDP by 2010."
He said the EU proposals would be unworkable, unfair and would be "ineffective as a response to climate change".
